raw_case_text: Male, 24-years-old, Caucasian, unemployed, from Tancredo Neves, State of Bahia, Brazil, was admitted to the University Hospital, in January 2012, presenting diffuse bullous lesions on the body, osteoarthritis of the distal interphalangeal joints and proteinuria 399 mg/day (reference value >150mg/day). He was diagnosed with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and treated with mycophenolate mofetil (MMF). The starting dose for MMF was 0.5 g per day and it was increased up to 1 g per day intravenously. In 2014, two years after SLE diagnosis, he was hospitalized, presenting with ulcerated-painless-skin lesions on the face, upper lip, scalp, neck, upper and lower limbs. Oral examination evidenced crusty upper lip lesions, poor oral health status and amelogenesis imperfecta ( Figure 1a and 1b). He developed secondary infection associated with fever, and antibiotic therapy with cephalexin was initiated (1g/day) and a maintenance dose of prednisone (5 mg/day intravenously). On the third day, biopsies were performed on the left nasal mucosa and on the right lower limb lesions. The diagnosis of disseminated leishmaniasis was confirmed (positive PCR and Montenegro intradermal test). Liposomal amphotericin B was introduced on the fourth day of hospitalization at a dose of 150 mg/day up to a maximum dose of 2,400 mg. The patient treatment was followed-up for six months, and lesions were observed to have healed. One month later, during the follow-up for SLE, we observed new development of ulcerated skin lesions on the face and on the upper and lower right limbs. Blisters and fever were absent and the recurrence of disseminated leishmaniasis was confirmed. Few weeks later, the patient was admitted for treatment of new lesions, presenting with erythema, diffuse facial edema, lymphadenopathy and ulcerated and pustular lesions. Patient was treated with liposomal amphotericin B at a cumulative dose of 3,050 mg and followed-up until complete remission of the lesions. Currently, patient is under maintenance treatment for SLE.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 26-year-old male with systemic lupus erythematosus presented with extensive, painless ulcerated skin lesions on his face, upper lip, scalp, neck, and extremities.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 26-year-old male diagnosed with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) in 2012 (presenting with bullous lesions, osteoarthritis, and proteinuria, treated with mycophenolate mofetil). In 2014, he was hospitalized with painless ulcerated skin lesions distributed across his face, upper lip, scalp, neck, and upper and lower limbs. He developed secondary bacterial infection with fever, which was managed with cephalexin (1 g/day) and maintenance prednisone (5 mg/day). On hospital day 3, biopsies of the nasal mucosa and lower limb lesions were obtained. Following initial resolution on liposomal amphotericin B, he experienced a disease relapse 1 month later with new ulcerated lesions on his face and right limbs, followed weeks later by severe facial erythema, edema, lymphadenopathy, and pustular eruptions requiring readmission.
subjective.past_medical_history: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) diagnosed in 2012, maintained on mycophenolate mofetil (titrated from 0.5 g/day to 1 g/day IV) and prednisone; amelogenesis imperfecta; poor oral health. Resident of Tancredo Neves, Bahia, Brazil.
subjective.review_of_systems: Fever associated with secondary bacterial superinfection; painless ulcerated skin lesions. Home medications: mycophenolate mofetil, prednisone. Allergies: None documented.

objective.physical_examination: Dermatologic: painless ulcerated lesions on the face, upper lip, scalp, neck, and upper and lower extremities. Oral: crusty upper lip lesions, amelogenesis imperfecta, poor dental status. Readmission examination: diffuse facial erythema, marked facial edema, regional lymphadenopathy, and ulcerated pustular lesions.
objective.routine_investigations: Urinalysis: proteinuria 399 mg/day (reference value >150 mg/day at initial SLE presentation).
objective.advanced_workup: Biopsies: incisional biopsies performed on the left nasal mucosa and right lower limb lesions.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Disseminated American tegumentary leishmaniasis in an immunosuppressed patient with systemic lupus erythematosus.
Diagnostic confirmation: Biopsies of nasal mucosa and lower limb lesions were confirmed by positive Leishmania polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and a positive Montenegro intradermal reaction (skin test).
Differentials ruled out: Bullous SLE flare, pemphigus vulgaris, disseminated fungal infection (paracoccidioidomycosis, histoplasmosis), cutaneous tuberculosis, and secondary bacterial ecthyma (treated with cephalexin).
Treatment and clinical course: Initially treated with intravenous liposomal amphotericin B (150 mg/day up to a cumulative dose of 2,400 mg) alongside cephalexin and maintenance prednisone, achieving complete lesion healing at 6 months. For disease relapse, he received a second course of liposomal amphotericin B to a cumulative dose of 3,050 mg, resulting in complete lesion remission while remaining on maintenance therapy for SLE.
